names.name: Casino Magic Biloxi
names.operator: Casino Magic Corp. (1993-Oct 1998); Hollywood Park, Inc./Pinnacle Entertainment (1998-2005)
names.note: Opened June 5, 1993 as the second Casino Magic casino; company bought for $340 million in October 1998; casino barge destroyed by Hurricane Katrina in 2005 and never reopened

names.name: Casino Magic Biloxi (Harrah's-owned, closed)
names.operator: Harrah's Entertainment (after Pinnacle handed over the property with $25 million)
names.note: Planned Margaritaville casino resort suspended 2008; hotel tower declared blighted

names.name: Margaritaville Resort Biloxi
names.note: Non-gaming hotel on the old site, opened June 23, 2016

label.basis: The sources opened show a corporate operator history; the only items found are a 1998 regulator-to-industry revolving-door report and a Biloxi Dixie Mafia case about illegal vice, neither of which ties the casino to organised crime.

venues.corrections: Opening year is 1993 (opened June 5, 1993), not 1992; 1992 is the year of the company's Bay St. Louis casino. The casino closed for good in 2005 (Katrina); closed is not null. The current resort is a non-gaming hotel.

names.name: Broadwater Beach Hotel / Broadwater Beach Resort
names.operator: Pete Martin Sr.; Joe Brown (from 1958); Dorothy Brown
names.note: Pre-casino resort; illegal gambling under the first owner; Hurricane Camille 1969

names.name: President Casino Broadwater Resort
names.operator: President Casinos (John E. Connelly); Broadwater Development LLC (from April 2005)
names.note: Riverboat opened August 1992, replaced by a barge in 1995; bankruptcy 2002; destroyed by Katrina August 29, 2005; barge sold to a Silver Slipper venture

label.basis: The history opened describes a bankruptcy-driven business story for the casino era; earlier illegal gambling (1939) is a pre-casino vice story, and the Halat Dixie Mafia case concerns Biloxi vice, not this property.

names.name: Boomtown New Orleans
names.operator: Pinnacle Entertainment; owned by Gaming and Leisure Properties since 2016 (leased back to Pinnacle); Penn Entertainment licence holder
names.note: Became largest riverboat in the region after taking a River City Casino riverboat in 1998

label.basis: Wikipedia history shows publicly traded corporate operators only; no organised-crime source found, but no gaming-board or court records could be opened.

venues.corrections: The name was Boomtown Westbank until 2002 (infobox 1994-2002).

names.name: Treasure Chest Casino
names.operator: Local investors with Boyd Gaming holding 15% (1994); Boyd Gaming 100% (from 1997)
names.note: Riverboat in Kenner opened 1994; Boyd bought out the investors in 1997

label.basis: I could not open any source on this casino that bears on organised crime; a search result suggested the Fifth Circuit Edwards opinion has a "Treasure Chest scheme" (public corruption in licensing) but the opinion could not be opened (blocked), so nothing is claimed.

venues.corrections: Current label none is not backed by a source I could open; mark unsupported until the Edwards opinion is read.

names.name: Imperial Palace Hotel and Casino Biloxi
names.operator: Ralph Engelstad; his estate trustees after 2002
names.note: Opened Dec 22, 1997; sister of the Las Vegas Imperial Palace

label.basis: The only regulatory action found on the founder is a 1989 Nevada fine for Hitler-birthday parties at his Las Vegas casino, a reputational matter, not organised crime.

names.name: Beau Rivage
names.operator: Mirage Resorts (Steve Wynn); MGM Mirage/MGM Resorts operator; MGM Growth Properties owner 2016; now Vici Properties
names.note: Opened March 1999; Katrina 2005, fully reopened Aug 29, 2006

label.basis: The Wikipedia history shows a corporate developer and no organised-crime material; I opened no regulatory or court records.

names.name: Harrah's Jazz (temporary casino)
names.note: Temporary casino 1995; bankruptcy filed in November 1995; project taken over by Harrah's

names.name: Harrah's New Orleans
names.operator: Harrah's Entertainment/Caesars Entertainment; Eldorado Resorts (2020); real estate to Vici Properties
names.note: Opened late October 1999; closed after Katrina, reopened Feb 17, 2006

label.basis: The history opened shows corporate and political licensing dealings (1993 joint venture under pressure from the governor) and no organised-crime link.

venues.corrections: The permanent casino opened in 1999, but the licence holder ran a temporary casino from 1995.

names.name: Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Biloxi
names.operator: Premier Entertainment Biloxi LLC (Leucadia National) 2002-2014; Twin River Worldwide Holdings/Bally's 2014-; Gaming and Leisure Properties owner since Jan 4, 2023
names.note: Soft opening June 30, grand opening July 7, 2007 after a Katrina delay; on the former Gold Shore Casino site

label.basis: A corporate and franchise history only; nothing on organised crime found, but I opened no regulatory records.

names.name: Isle of Capri Biloxi
names.operator: Isle of Capri Casinos (Bernard Goldstein's company)
names.note: First casino in Biloxi, August 1992; casino destroyed by Katrina in 2005

names.name: Golden Nugget Biloxi
names.note: Sold 2012 and converted to a Golden Nugget

label.basis: The histories opened show a corporate operator chain only; nothing found on organised crime.

venues.corrections: Opening year is 1992 (as Isle of Capri); 2012 is the rebrand. The current summary (Guy McAfee, 1946, Steve Wynn) describes the Las Vegas Golden Nugget, not this Biloxi property.

gaps: Official sources (Mississippi Gaming Commission, Louisiana Gaming Control Board, PEER report, FBI, OJP) were refused by the proxy; no gaming-board record could be opened for any venue.

United States v. Edwards, 303 F.3d 606 (5th Cir. 2002): justia (Cloudflare), ca5.uscourts.gov, findlaw, courtlistener and archive.org were all unavailable, so the Treasure Chest scheme could not be checked. Recalled, not fetched: that opinion names a "Treasure Chest scheme".
Treasure Chest: names of the original local investors, and the 2024 move from the riverboat to land, are not backed by a page I opened.
IP Casino Biloxi: closure or later ownership after Boyd (2011) not checked.
All dates and lineages rest on Wikipedia as secondary context; no operator filings were opened.
Beau Rivage: the Mirage-MGM merger date (2000) is not stated in a page I opened.
